In the repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (currently on branch feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info, whose HEAD is develop's tip 8362b3c = "Merge pull request #59"), audit what PR #59 established as the UI build pattern.

PR #59 was the SFCC-55 global footer UI build. Its commits are everything between cd68e97 and 8362b3c on develop.

Investigate and report, with file:line evidence:

1. COMPONENT STRUCTURE — the exact folder/file layout used for atoms, molecules and organisms under overrides/app/components/ui-kits/. What files does each component consistently have? When does one get a `<name>.css.ts` recipe and when not?

2. STYLING — how recipes are authored (parts, baseStyle, variants, resolver functions), how they are registered, how tokens are referenced (var(--zimm-*) vs bare keys), where responsive steps live, how provisional/unsourced values are annotated.

3. ENFORCEMENT — what mechanically enforces these conventions. Read overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts closely and list every rule it actually enforces and what it cannot see. Note any other guards.

4. TESTING SHAPE — for each ui-kits component #59 added, list which of {index.stories.tsx with play, index.test.tsx, <name>.css.test.ts} it has, and infer the rule being followed. Read overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx as the stated reference pattern and describe precisely what it does and does not assert.

5. SHARED UTILITIES AND HOOKS #59 introduced that a new feature should reuse rather than rebuild — e.g. useUiCopy, safeHref, resolveByRegion, fontFace, uiCopyProvider, footerShared. For each, state its purpose and the call-site convention.

6. Anything else #59 established that a developer building a NEW page/component in this repo would be expected to follow.

Be concrete and quote code. This is an independent audit — do not assume anything is correct just because it exists. Report back; do not edit anything.

3	export type UiCopyContextValue = {
4	  /**
5	   * Returns the CMS value for `key`, or `fallback` while the fetch is loading, on fetch
6	   * error, or when no `uiCopy` entry with that key exists yet.
7	   */
8	  t: (key: string, fallback: string) => string;
9	  isLoading: boolean;
10	};
11	
12	/**
13	 * Populated by UiCopyProvider (overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider), mounted once in
14	 * _app-config. Not meant to be consumed directly — call useUiCopy() instead, which supplies
15	 * the no-Provider fallback.
16	 */
17	export const UiCopyContext = createContext<UiCopyContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
18	
19	const FALLBACK_ONLY: UiCopyContextValue = {
20	  t: (_key: string, fallback: string) => fallback,
21	  isLoading: false,
22	};
23	
24	/**
25	 * App-wide UI-copy lookup, backed by Contentful's uiCopy content type — one entry per string,
26	 * fetched in a single bulk call by UiCopyProvider and shared via context, the same pattern
27	 * this app already uses for translations (`useIntl`) rather than the per-page container-fetch
28	 * pattern commerce-sdk-react hooks use. uiCopy is app-wide static content, not page-specific
29	 * business data, so it's safe to call from any component — including presentational leaves —
30	 * without threading it through as a prop.
31	 *
32	 * Safe to call with no UiCopyProvider mounted above it (Storybook, an isolated unit test):
33	 * degrades to fallback-only text instead of throwing, so every call site stays functional and
34	 * testable with zero setup.
35	 *
36	 * @returns `t` lookup function plus `isLoading`
37	 */
38	export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;

1	/**
2	 * Allow-list guard for hrefs that originate outside the codebase.
3	 *
4	 * Anything reaching an `href` from Contentful, a URL parameter, or a prop supplied by a
5	 * caller we do not control has to pass through here first. `javascript:` and `data:` URLs
6	 * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
7	 * lookahead rejects that, including the backslash form — a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`,
8	 * so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as a second slash is. `e9c2180` closed
9	 * only the forward-slash half; the backslash and control-character forms stayed open until now.
10	 *
11	 * Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a deny-list has to anticipate every scheme,
12	 * and browsers keep adding them.
13	 */
14	// eslint-disable no-control-regex — the control characters ARE the subject here. The rule exists
15	// to catch them appearing by accident; these are deliberate, and matching them is the whole point
16	// of the fix. Suppressed at the point of use rather than in .eslintrc, per the escape-hatch
17	// convention in .claude/rules/typescript.md.
18	/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
19	const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
20	const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
21	/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
22	
23	/**
24	 * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
25	 *
26	 * The WHATWG parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
27	 * in the input, BEFORE it parses. `/\u0009/evil.com` is therefore parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing
28	 * the raw string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves — which
29	 * is exactly how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open.
30	 *
31	 * A plain space is deliberately not stripped: the parser percent-encodes it rather than removing
32	 * it, so `/ /evil.com` resolves on-site and must stay allowed.
33	 */
34	const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
35	
36	const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
37	
38	/** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
39	export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the BrowserStack Automate suite scoped to one Jira story, the same
# way e2e-browserstack does on a PR — lets a developer execute their
# feature-branch story locally before pushing, using real BrowserStack
# (see .claude/rules/testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping).
#
# Usage:
#   npm run test:story                  # auto-detects the Jira key(s)
#   npm run test:story -- SFCC-142      # explicit key(s), space-separated
#
# Auto-detection scans commit messages on this branch (commits ahead of
# origin/develop) and the branch name for SFCC-NNN — the same SFCC-[0-9]+
# pattern qa.yml's "Detect Jira story keys" step uses for a PR's title/body/
# branch. Kept as a literal duplicate there rather than a shared script:
# it's one regex, and the input sources genuinely differ (PR text vs local
# git state) — update both if the Jira project key prefix ever changes.
#
# Exit code: 0 if BrowserStack ran (regardless of test pass/fail — that's
# BrowserStack's own exit code), 1 if no Jira key was found or a required
# env var is missing.

set -euo pipefail

ENV_FILE=".env"

if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    set -a && source "$ENV_FILE" && set +a
fi

KEYS="$*"

if [[ -z "$KEYS" ]]; then
    BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/develop 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [[ -n "$BASE" ]]; then
        COMMIT_MSGS=$(git log "$BASE"..HEAD --pretty=%B 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    else
        COMMIT_MSGS=""
    fi
    BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
=== PRE-PUSH ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
#
# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
#
# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
#
# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
status=0

while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
  case "$remote_ref" in
    refs/tags/v*)
      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
        status=1
      fi
      ;;
  esac
done

exit $status

# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
which is what `audit:tokens` is for.

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where

  FavouritesIcon,
  FavouritesSolidIcon,
  PhoneIcon,
  WhatsAppIcon,
  EmailIcon,
} from 'app/components/icons';

// Figma iconography spec: node 1892:59595 — 34 of 34 types implemented.
export type ZimmIconType =
  | 'arrow-down'
  | 'arrow-link'
  | 'arrow-up'
  | 'bag'
  | 'bag-selected'
  | 'calendar'
  | 'carousel'
  | 'carousel-selected'
  | 'chat'
  | 'check'
  | 'chevron-down'
  | 'chevron-left'
  | 'chevron-right'
  | 'chevron-up'
  | 'close'

  | 'wishlist'
  | 'wishlist-selected'
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  | 'phone'
  | 'whatsapp'
  | 'email';

export type ZimmIconSize = keyof typeof iconSizes;

type ZimmIconProps = {
  type: ZimmIconType;
  size?: ZimmIconSize;
  /** Pass Chakra token strings or CSS keywords (e.g. 'text.primary', 'currentColor').
   *  Do not pass hardcoded hex values — use theme tokens. */
  color?: string;
} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });

const ICON_MAP = {
  'arrow-down': ArrowDownIcon,
  'arrow-link': ArrowLinkIcon,
  'arrow-up': ArrowUpIcon,
  bag: BagIcon,
  'bag-selected': BagSelectedIcon,
  calendar: CalendarIcon,
  carousel: CarouselIcon,
  'carousel-selected': CarouselSelectedIcon,
  chat: ChatIcon,
  check: CheckIcon,
  'chevron-down': ChevronDownIcon,
  'chevron-left': ChevronLeftIcon,
  'chevron-right': ChevronRightIcon,
  'chevron-up': ChevronUpIcon,
  close: CloseIcon,
  delete: DeleteIcon,
  edit: EditIcon,
  'external-link': ExternalLinkIcon,
  info: InfoIcon,
  'info-selected': InfoSelectedIcon,
  location: LocationIcon,
  menu: MenuIcon,
  minus: MinusIcon,
  mute: MuteIcon,
  password: PasswordShowIcon,
  pause: PauseIcon,
  play: PlayIcon,
  plus: PlusIcon,
  profile: ProfileIcon,
  search: SearchIcon,
  share: ShareIcon,
  'share-2': ShareTwoIcon,
  wishlist: FavouritesIcon,
  'wishlist-selected': FavouritesSolidIcon,

  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  phone: PhoneIcon,
  whatsapp: WhatsAppIcon,
  email: EmailIcon,
} as const;

export const ZimmIcon = ({ type, size = 'md', color = 'currentColor', ...aria }: ZimmIconProps) => {
  const Icon = ICON_MAP[type];

      boxSize={iconSizes[size]}
      color={color}
      aria-hidden={ariaHidden}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
    />
  );
};

## 2. STYLING

### Recipe authoring — three shapes

**(a) Single-part, `defineStyleConfig`:**
```ts
// zimmNavItem.css.ts:74
export const ZimmNavItem = defineStyleConfig({ baseStyle, variants, defaultProps: { variant: 'light' } });
```
Also `zimmButton.css.ts:243` (`baseStyle`, `variants`, `sizes`, `defaultProps`). Consumed via `useStyleConfig('ZimmNavItem', { variant })` — `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:33`.

**(b) Multipart — a plain object literal, NOT `createMultiStyleConfigHelpers`:**
```ts
// zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:1
export const ZimmContactIconRow = {
  parts: ['row', 'iconLink'],
  baseStyle: { … },
};
```
Every multipart recipe in #59 uses this bare-object form: `zimmModal.css.ts:5`, `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts:3`, `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:14`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:77`, `footer.css.ts:20`, `footerNavColumn.css.ts:3`. Consumed with `useMultiStyleConfig`. No `defineMultiStyleConfig`, no `anatomy`, no type on the recipe object.

**(c) Function-form `baseStyle` for state cascades** — only where the theme has to branch on React state:
```ts
// zimmTextInput.css.ts:79
baseStyle: (props: ZimmTextInputStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => { … }
```
State is fed in at the call site — `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:80-86` passes `{ inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled: value.length > 0 }`. The prop type is **exported from the recipe file** (`zimmTextInput.css.ts:43`) so tests can import it.

### Resolver functions

Pure, exported, named `resolve<Thing>`, with the precedence stated in a one-line JSDoc:
```ts
// zimmTextInput.css.ts:54-55
/** Border colour precedence: disabled > error > focus > filled > default. */
export const resolveBorderColour = ({ inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled }) => { … }
```
Also `resolveHoverBorderColour:65`, `resolveLabelColour:70`. They are exported **specifically so they can be unit-tested without rendering** — `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:2` imports all three. The commit `3220239` ("move colour derivation from the hook into the theme recipe") is the decision: derivation lives in the recipe, not the hook.

### Registration

Manual, one file: `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:1-35`. Every recipe imported by path, then listed in the `components` object. The object key is the string passed to `useStyleConfig`/`useMultiStyleConfig` — Chakra resolves by key, not by file path.

**Call-site convention: name the key.**
```ts
// zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:8
const ZIMM_SUBSCRIBE_SECTION_RECIPE = 'ZimmSubscribeSection';
…
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_SUBSCRIBE_SECTION_RECIPE, {});
```
Followed by 7 of 9 call sites (`zimmContactIconRow:6`, `zimmModal:5`, `zimmSubscribeModal:9-10`, `footer/index.tsx:15`, `footerNavColumn:7`, `bottomBar:7`). **Not** followed by `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:80` or `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:33`, which pass raw strings. The convention is real but was never retro-applied.

### Tokens: `var(--zimm-*)`, never a bare key

The house rule is `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2, restated in `css.md`. It is explicitly *not* a correctness rule — `theme.colors` and `theme.space` **are** registered (`theme/index.ts:52-58`), so a bare key resolves to the same value. The reason given is reviewer legibility: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is unambiguous at the call site; a bare key forces the reviewer to recall which scales are registered (`theme/index.ts:26-49` lists the deliberately-unregistered ones: `fontSizes`, `transition`, `sizes`).

Sanctioned exceptions, all present in #59 code:
- `textStyle: 'button' | 'navigation' | 'caption' | 'body2' | 'heading3'` — bare by necessity; there is no `var()` form for the composite expansion. `css.md` states this explicitly.
- `zIndex: 'overlay'` (`zimmModal.css.ts:21`) — a bare token key on a registered scale. Passes only because no guard covers `zIndex` (see §3).
- `useToken('colors', ['text.inverse', 'text.default'])` (`zimmLogo/index.tsx:23`) — bare keys via the JS API, justified inline: an SVG `fill` attribute needs a concrete colour, not a custom-property reference.

### Responsive steps

**Raw media queries keyed off a shared `BP` object. Chakra's array shorthand is banned.**
```ts
// footer.css.ts:43
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { flexDirection: 'row', gap: 0, … },
```
Also `footer.css.ts:54, 62, 65, 77, 82, 85, 120` and `footerNavColumn.css.ts:34`. `overrideStyling.md` gives the reason: the array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key back at every step, and the guard walks responsive arrays attributing each element to the same prop — all four would fail.

`BP` lives in `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts:18-22` and is the **one deliberate place a theme file imports `foundation/` directly** (`import { breakpoints } from '../foundation/gridSystem'`, line 1) — because media queries cannot consume `var()`. It carries an explicit `audit-allow:` marker (line 15) for the raw `em` values.

### Provisional / unsourced values

Pattern: **named UPPER_SNAKE constant at the top of the file + a comment containing one of four magic words.**

```ts
// zimmButton.css.ts:200-207
// PROVISIONAL prototype button dimensions. The Handover's action tokens specify 52px (lg) /
// 40px (md) … pending sign-off …
const BTN_HEIGHT_LG = '50px';
```

Instances: `footer.css.ts:3-13` (four constants under one shared comment), `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:1-12`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts:3-11` (`NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y = '4.5px'`), `zimmTextInput.css.ts:26-38`, `footerShared.ts:28`, `zimmLogo/index.tsx:9-13`.

**The four words are mechanically load-bearing:** `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:59` — `EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE = /provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i`, matched against the contiguous non-blank block ending at the offending line (`auditTokenUsage.mjs:119-122`). Consequence a new developer will hit: **inserting a blank line between the explanatory comment and the constant silently converts an acknowledged exception into a build failure** for that script.

Secondary convention: Figma provenance cited inline as node IDs — `zimmTextInput.css.ts:3` (`node 40000265:374`), `footer.css.ts:36-37`, `footerNavColumn.css.ts:8`, `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:17`.

## 3. ENFORCEMENT

### `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` — every rule it enforces

Six tests. In order:

**1. `collect() actually walks the registered recipes` (:287)** — a vacuity guard.
```ts
expect(Object.keys(components).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
expect(collect().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
```
Added by `e686bd3`. Without it, deleting `components` turns the whole file green, since every other test asserts an empty offender list.

**2. `no sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key` (:295)** — `SIZING_PROPS` (13 names, :118-132: `width/height/min*/max*/boxSize/w/h/minW/…`) × `Object.keys(spacing)`. Catches the real shipped bug: `width: 'xl'` reads Chakra's `sizes.xl` = 36rem = 576px, because the Zimmermann scale is registered as `space` only.

**3. `no typography property uses a bare scale key` (:305)** — `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` (:153-157) maps `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` each to *(its own Zimmermann scale keys ∪ the spacing keys)*. `fontWeight` is deliberately excluded (:150-151): `medium` is a key in both scales and resolves to 500 either way.

**4. `no compound shorthand contains a bare scale key` (:315)** — for `SPACE_SHORTHANDS` (`padding/margin/inset/gap/p/m`, :160), only when the value contains whitespace; `var(…)` is masked out first (:321) before splitting. Catches `padding: 'xs 0'`, which Chakra emits verbatim and the browser drops.

**5. `no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale` (:331)** — the house-style guard. `SPACE_PROPS` (44 names, :70-113, including logical/directional variants and `top/left/right/bottom`) × spacing keys, OR `COLOR_PROPS` (8 names, :116) × the recursively flattened colour paths (`flattenKeys`, :60-66, producing `'text.default'`, `'action.primary.bgDefault'`, …). This is the one that makes `var(--zimm-*)` mandatory.

**6. `no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name` (:347)** — for each registered key not in `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` (:351), compares our `baseStyle` keys against the composed `theme.components[name]` keys; any key present after composition that we never declared came from the base theme.

**Walk mechanics worth knowing before you write a recipe:**
- Only three sections are walked: `resolveAllBaseStyles(r)` (all 2⁵ = 32 boolean prop combinations, :236-243, :267) plus `r.variants` and `r.sizes` (:270-272).
- `walk` reports **string leaves only** (:199). Numbers (`flex: 1`, `opacity: 0.4`) are invisible.
- `isResponsiveContainer` (:181) requires **all** keys be breakpoints, not any — because `xl`/`2xl` are keys in both `breakpoints` and `spacing`, and `sm`/`md`/`lg` in both `breakpoints` and the typography scales (:170-179).
- Offenders are de-duplicated by the rendered `where()` string (:277-283), since 32 resolutions produce 32 copies of every prop-independent line.

### What `recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot see

The file names two blind spots itself (:36-43). I confirmed those and found more.

**a) JSX / `sx` / `style` props — self-declared.** Its SCOPE note cites `header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) as unreachable. **Two live instances still exist in #59's own code:** `zimmTextInput/index.stories.tsx:103` and `:119` — `<Box bg="background.05" p="xl">` — a bare colour key *and* a bare space key, precisely what test 5 forbids inside a recipe. `background.05` is a real registered key (`foundation/colour.ts:49-57`), so it renders correctly; it just violates the stated house rule where nothing can see it.

**b) Any style object outside the registry.** `collect()` iterates `Object.entries(components)` (:265). `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:60`'s inline `__css` is a style object with no recipe, so it is structurally outside the guard.

**c) A recipe file that was never registered.** Nothing asserts that every `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` appears in `theme/components/index.ts`. A new component whose recipe is authored but not registered gets **zero guard coverage and renders unstyled** — `useMultiStyleConfig` on an unknown key returns an empty object, and `__css={undefined}` is legal.

**d) A function-form `baseStyle` branching on a prop name not in the fixed list.** `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS` (:217-225) hardcodes `inverse/disabled/hasError/focused/filled`. `PROP_COMBINATIONS` enumerates combinations of *those* keys only. A new recipe branching on `selected`, `compact`, `size`, etc. resolves it as `undefined` across all 32 combinations, so **only the falsy branch is ever walked**. The file's own comment (:227-235) documents that this exact class of miss let `'3xs'` ship — but the fix enumerated combinations of the *known* keys rather than deriving them from the recipe, so the hole reopens for the next new prop name. This is the single most likely way a new component gets false-green coverage.

**e) A function-form `variants` or `sizes`.** `collect()` passes `r.variants`/`r.sizes` straight to `walk` (:271); `walk` returns early on a non-object (:192). Chakra supports `variants: { x: (props) => ({…}) }`; such a variant is silently skipped entirely.

**f) The namespacing guard only compares top-level `baseStyle` keys** (:358-360). For a multipart recipe those keys are *part names* — so a base SFCC recipe sharing a part name deep-merges *inside* that part and is not flagged. It also never inspects `variants` or `sizes` for inherited entries, which is exactly the "a key you add that the base lacks is appended last" hazard its own header describes (:20-22).

**g) Scales with no prop list.** `zIndex`, `borderRadius`, `borderWidth`, `boxShadow`, `fontFamily`, `transition` appear in none of the five prop sets. `zimmModal.css.ts:21`'s `zIndex: 'overlay'` is a live bare token key that passes clean.

**h) Raw hex/px/rem/em literals** — explicitly not this test's job.

**`useUiCopy`** — `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts:38`
CMS-backed microcopy lookup. Call convention: `const { t } = useUiCopy(); t('footer.subscribe.emailLabel', 'Email')` — dotted namespace key, **mandatory** English fallback as the second argument. **`UiCopyProvider`** — `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:18`
Mounted **once**, in `_app-config/index.tsx` inside `ChakraProvider`. One bulk `useContentfulEntries<UiCopyEntry>('uiCopy')` call for the whole app. Fallback-on-failure by design (:29-32), explicitly contrasted with structural content (which renders nothing rather than substitute placeholders). Don't add a second one.

**`isSafeHref`** — `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts:39`
Allow-list guard for any href not authored in the codebase (Contentful, URL params, untrusted props). `SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i` applied *after* WHATWG-style normalisation (:34) — the normalisation is the point, since testing the raw string is how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open. Call-site convention: the false branch renders a **labelled non-interactive `<span>`** (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:75-88`) or a `<button>` (`zimmNavItem/index.tsx:34+`) — never nothing, never a dead `<a>`.

Generic over any Contentful entry carrying `fields.regions`; not footer-specific. `filterByRegion` for arrays where several regional entries legitimately coexist; `pickMostSpecificByRegion` for a single winner. Fewer regions = more specific; omitted/empty = global and least specific. Ties resolve by `sys.updatedAt` then `sys.id` with a `console.warn` on every tie (:77-79) — deliberately order-independent, because `getEntries` is called with no `order`. Call-site convention: fetch → pick the root entry → map nested arrays through `filterByRegion` — `footer/index.tsx:144-156` (`scopeToRegion`) and `:202-203`.

Declares the two self-hosted Futura Round faces. **Already mounted in both** `_app-config/index.tsx` and `.storybook/preview.tsx` — a new feature must not add another. **`footerShared`** — `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts`
Exports `BP` (:18) and `SIZE_COL_NAV` (:28). Scope is explicitly footer-only (:6). The **pattern** generalises and is the thing to reuse: cross-file values shared by a decomposed feature's recipes go in a small `theme/components/<feature>Shared.ts`, never copy-pasted into each `.css.ts`. A new page should create its own analogue rather than import `footerShared`.

**Also reusable, added by #59:** `useZimmModal` (`overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.ts` — focus trap, portal mount, scroll lock, paired with the `ZimmModal` atom), `useZimmTextInputState`, `useSubscribeSection`. All three have sibling test files.

## 6. Anything else a new page/component is expected to follow

**Hooks are flat, not co-located.** `overrides/app/hooks/use<X>.ts`, camelCase, with a sibling `use<X>.test.ts(x)`. #59 added 4 hooks and 4 hook tests — 4/4. That's markedly higher discipline than the components got (1/10). The naming convention in `components.md` is `use<ComponentName><Feature>` (`useSubscribeSection`, `useZimmTextInputState`, `useZimmModal`).

**Container/presentational split, in one file.** Named export = presentational, takes `data` as a **required** prop, fetches nothing (`footer/index.tsx:68`). Default export = container that owns the fetch (`FooterContainer`, `:172`; `export default`, `:219`). Note the PR's own honest caveat at `:168-170`: this puts a fetch inside `components/`, which `components.md` reserves for containers — an acknowledged deviation forced by base `_app` rendering `<Footer />` with no props, **not** a pattern to copy uncritically.

**Story fixtures go in a separate file.** `footer/index.stories.content.ts` holds `FOOTER_FIXTURE`, so `index.stories.tsx` stays presentation. Referenced from the prop JSDoc at `footer/index.tsx:33`.

**Storybook dark-surface decorator convention — and a live contradiction.** `zimmSubscribeSection/index.stories.tsx:17-30`: reproduce the shipped background in the meta `decorators`, using the same `var(--zimm-*)` token the component renders against. The comment explains that `parameters: { backgrounds: { default: 'dark' } }` is a **silent no-op** in Storybook 10 (it reads `globals.backgrounds.value`), and that the built-in `dark` (#333) would introduce a second underived dark that can drift from the token. **`zimmContactIconRow/index.stories.tsx:9` still uses exactly that no-op form** — the fix was applied in one file and not the other. Use the decorator.

**A11y is written into the code with the success criterion cited.** SC 2.5.8 24px minimum targets (`zimmButton.css.ts:226-240`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:151-154`, `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:11-16`); SC 2.4.7 visible focus on every interactive part, never `outline: none` (`zimmButton.css.ts:33-37`, `footer.css.ts:135-139`); SC 3.2.5 new-tab disclosure in the accessible name (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:39-40`); SC 1.4.4 `rem` for anything holding text (`zimmTextInput.css.ts:26-36`, `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:10-11`). Contrast decisions are stated with the measured ratio (`zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts:14-15`: *"text.muted (#969696) would fail WCAG AA 4.5:1 at 12px on the white modal panel"*).

**Import style is inconsistent — prefer absolute.** `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:3-5` uses `'../../atoms/zimmTextInput'`; `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:3-4` uses `'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmInputAction'`. Absolute `app/...` is the majority form and matches how tests write `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon')`. Nothing enforces either.

**Comment culture is the loudest unwritten rule.** Every non-obvious value carries a *why*, the rejected alternative, and the specific defect the current form fixed — e.g. `footerNavColumn.css.ts:63-68` (the 1.5px `<li>` line-box leak that made the column 9px taller than Figma), `zimmTextInput.css.ts:26-35` (px → rem because at 200% zoom the slot reached 90px against a 53px field), `zimmButton.css.ts:226-235` (why `minW/minH` and not padding — `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a style prop, which merges after `__css`). Not mechanically enforced, but a component written without it will not look like it belongs.

**The registry is machine-generated from your JSDoc.** `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` regenerates `.claude/registry/components.md` on any `components/` change, pulling the one-line JSDoc and the props type verbatim (see `.claude/registry/components.md:86-95`). So `/** Atom — … */`, `/** Molecule — … */`, `/** Organism — … */` above the export is consumed by tooling, not decoration.

**Storybook build prerequisites #59 introduced.** `.storybook/main.js` now sets `staticDirs: [{ from: '../overrides/app/static', to: '/static' }]` and pushes a `DefinePlugin({ WEBPACK_TARGET: "'web'" })` — the latter is required for anything reaching `ssr-config` (e.g. a story that imports `app/config/contentful.ts`) to resolve the browser-safe branch. A new story that pulls in config will silently break the browser bundle without it.

### Three things I would not assume are correct

1. **The testing rule merged in #59 is not the testing shape merged in #59.** 1 of 10 ui-kits components has an `index.test.tsx`; two components with real branching have none. Follow the rule text, not the neighbours.
2. **`recipeGuards.test.ts`'s hardcoded `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS` (:217-225) is the guard's weakest joint.** A new function-form recipe branching on any prop name outside `inverse/disabled/hasError/focused/filled` gets only its falsy branch walked, and will report green.
3. **Nothing verifies that a `.css.ts` you write is registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.** Forget that line and the component renders unstyled *and* invisible to every guard.
